title: Rafi and the Rolling Pumpkins
markdown:
Bright sunshine streamed through Rafi’s window. Birds chirped. He bounced out of bed, grabbed his propeller cap, and dashed outside. Plum, his rabbit friend, twitched her nose.

“Plum! Look!”

A cart piled high with big bright pumpkins sat stuck in the garden path. It would not budge. One pumpkin leaned as if it wanted to escape and then thought better of it.

“Oh my!” Plum nudged a pumpkin. It wobbled. The cart stayed put, wheels half hidden in a dip of dirt.

Rafi gripped the handles. “Push, Plum! Together!” They pushed and pulled, puffing hard. The cart clunked, inched, stopped. “The pumpkins are too heavy!”

Mr. Reed, the wise badger, ambled over. “A sticky situation?”

“We can’t move it! Too heavy!”

Reed peered under, not at the pile. “You’re pushing the whole cart. Look at what’s helping it sit up.”

Rafi and Plum tilted their heads. Round black things underneath, dusty, waiting.

“Wheels!” Plum squeaked.

“Exactly. They roll around and around. Heavy pumpkins glide. Much easier than sliding the bottom along the dirt.”

Rafi watched a wheel. Spin, spin, spin — once he freed it from the dip with a wriggle of the cart. The heavy load remembered how to move. “The wheels!”

He gave a gentle push by a wheel, not a desperate shove on the handles alone. WHOOSH. The cart glided, picking up speed. Smooth whirring filled the air. Plum giggled and hopped alongside, ears streaming. “So easy now!”

“Wheels help us move big heavy things.” They rolled the cart to the pumpkin patch without puffing, Rafi steering around a flowerpot, Plum calling left and right as if she were a very small captain.

He did not wonder what other inventions waited. He parked the cart where Reed pointed, set the brake stone, and took off the propeller cap so it would not catch in the spokes. Plum sat on the path and twitched at a pumpkin that had behaved, at last, like cargo.
